skill.name: wp-playground
skill.description: Guides disposable WordPress Playground environments, local project mounts, blueprints, snapshots, version testing, and Xdebug workflows in browsers or through the CLI.
skill.summary: Create reproducible WordPress test environments without maintaining a full local stack.
skill.author: Automattic

security_audit.summary: Static alerts for hardcoded URLs and Markdown backticks are false positives involving official endpoints, localhost, options, and documented commands. Two contextual risks remain: unpinned npx package execution and powerful remote blueprints without explicit trust checks. No prompt injection, credential collection, or covert exfiltration behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Examples execute an unpinned CLI package through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed CLI version and document lockfile or integrity verification instead of using the latest release.

remediation.issue: Remote blueprints may contain powerful PHP and filesystem steps.
remediation.suggestion: Require trusted origins, inspect every blueprint before execution, and forbid adjacent-file access for untrusted recipes.

content.user_title: Run Disposable WordPress Tests with Playground
content.value_statement: WordPress testing often requires slow local infrastructure and repeated setup. This skill guides disposable environments, reproducible blueprints, snapshots, version testing, and Xdebug workflows.
actual_capabilities: Starts disposable WordPress environments through the browser or local Playground CLI.
Mounts one or more local plugins, themes, or WordPress directories.
Runs trusted local or remote blueprints for scripted site setup.
Builds shareable snapshots for bug reports, demonstrations, or CI workflows.
Selects WordPress and PHP versions for focused compatibility testing.
Guides Xdebug setup, mount verification, smoke tests, and common troubleshooting.
limitations: Local CLI workflows require Node.js 20.18 or newer with npm and npx.
WebAssembly and SQLite cannot replace every native extension or external database workflow.
Playground instances are ephemeral unless you create and retain a snapshot.
Remote blueprints and packages using the latest tag require independent trust review.

use_cases.title: Test a WordPress plugin
use_cases.description: Mount a plugin into an isolated site, select target versions, activate it, and run focused smoke checks.

use_cases.title: Review a theme change
use_cases.description: Launch a disposable site with the theme mounted, verify activation, and reproduce visual or compatibility issues.

use_cases.title: Automate reproducible setup
use_cases.description: Run a reviewed blueprint, validate its steps, and build a snapshot for continuous integration or issue reproduction.

prompt_templates.title: Start a local test site
prompt_templates.prompt: Start WordPress Playground for my plugin at [path]. Check Node, auto-mount it, use WordPress [version], and explain verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Test version compatibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test matrix for [project] across WordPress [versions] and PHP [versions]. Provide isolated commands and smoke checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a blueprint workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a trusted Playground blueprint for [goal] using [assets]. Validate required steps, local file access, versions, and reproducible verification.

prompt_templates.title: Debug and package a reproduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Mount [project path], enable Xdebug, reproduce [issue], collect focused diagnostics, then build a shareable snapshot without secrets.

output_examples.input: Test my plugin on WordPress 6.9 with PHP 8.3.
output: A prerequisite check for Node.js and npm.
An auto-mount launch plan pinned to the requested versions.
Activation and smoke-test steps for the plugin.

output_examples.input: Create a repeatable demonstration site from trusted assets.
output: A blueprint plan covering versions, installation, activation, and verification.
A review step for asset origins and local file permissions.
A snapshot workflow for sharing the resulting site.

output_examples.input: My Playground Xdebug breakpoints are not triggered.
output: Checks for the active debug flag, listener port, and IDE key.
Path-mapping verification for the mounted virtual filesystem.
Focused debug logging and a fallback compatibility check.

best_practices: Pin reviewed CLI, WordPress, and PHP versions when reproducibility matters.
Inspect blueprint sources and powerful steps before running local or remote recipes.
Keep mounted directories free of secrets and verify activation with targeted smoke tests.
anti_patterns: Do not connect Playground workflows to production data or credentials.
Do not execute unreviewed remote blueprints or unpinned packages.
Do not assume ephemeral instances support every native extension or persistent database feature.

faq.question: Can I use WordPress Playground without Node.js?
faq.answer: Yes, browser workflows do not require Node.js. Local CLI workflows require Node.js 20.18 or newer.

faq.question: Does a Playground site persist automatically?
faq.answer: No. Treat instances as ephemeral and build a snapshot when you need a reusable result.

faq.question: Can it test both plugins and themes?
faq.answer: Yes. Auto-mount can detect a project, while explicit mounts support multiple plugins, themes, and custom directories.

faq.question: Can I choose WordPress and PHP versions?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI accepts WordPress and PHP version options for compatibility testing.

faq.question: Does the skill support Xdebug?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides debugger startup, IDE connection, path mapping, and logging. Flag names may vary by CLI release.

faq.question: Is Playground a production WordPress replacement?
faq.answer: No. WebAssembly, SQLite, and ephemeral storage make it suitable for testing, demonstrations, and reproducible issue investigation.
